390: // --- Frontier API key ------------------------------------------------------
391: 
392: // checkFrontierKeyFn validates the configured frontier API key by
393: // issuing a GET /v1/models with a Bearer header. A 200 means the
394: // key is accepted; 401/403 means the key is bad; any other status
395: // is reported as-is so the operator can investigate.
396: //
397: // When cfg.FrontierKey is empty we skip with a hint: the proxy still
398: // runs without a frontier key (local + fusion degrade), but any
399: // frontier-bound request will 401.
400: func checkFrontierKeyFn(ctx context.Context, cfg config.Config, opts Options) Check {
401: 	if !cfg.FrontierEnabled() {
402: 		return Check{
403: 			Name:   checkFrontierKey,
404: 			Status: StatusSkip,
405: 			Detail: "no NEXUS_FRONTIER_API_KEY set — frontier routing will return 401",
406: 		}
407: 	}
408: 	base, err := frontierBaseURL(cfg.FrontierURL)
409: 	if err != nil {
410: 		return Check{
411: 			Name:   checkFrontierKey,
412: 			Status: StatusFail,
413: 			Detail: fmt.Sprintf("invalid NEXUS_FRONTIER_URL %q: %v", cfg.FrontierURL, err),
414: 		}
415: 	}
416: 	target := strings.TrimRight(base, "/") + "/models"
417: 	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, opts.Timeout)
418: 	defer cancel()
419: 	req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodGet, target, nil)
420: 	if err != nil {
421: 		return Check{
422: 			Name:   checkFrontierKey,
423: 			Status: StatusFail,
424: 			Detail: err.Error(),
425: 		}
426: 	}
427: 	req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+cfg.FrontierKey)
428: 	resp, err := opts.HTTPClient.Do(req)
429: 	if err != nil {
430: 		return Check{
431: 			Name:   checkFrontierKey,
432: 			Status: StatusFail,
433: 			Detail: fmt.Sprintf("cannot reach %s: %v", target, err),
434: 		}
435: 	}
436: 	defer resp.Body.Close()
437: 	switch {
438: 	case resp.StatusCode == http.StatusOK:
439: 		return Check{
440: 			Name:   checkFrontierKey,
441: 			Status: StatusPass,
442: 			Detail: fmt.Sprintf("key accepted (endpoint: %s)", cfg.FrontierURL),
443: 		}
444: 	case resp.StatusCode == http.StatusUnauthorized, resp.StatusCode == http.StatusForbidden:
445: 		return Check{
446: 			Name:   checkFrontierKey,
447: 			Status: StatusFail,
448: 			Detail: fmt.Sprintf("endpoint rejected the key (status %d)", resp.StatusCode),
449: 		}
450: 	default:
451: 		return Check{
452: 			Name:   checkFrontierKey,
453: 			Status: StatusFail,
454: 			Detail: fmt.Sprintf("unexpected status %d from %s", resp.StatusCode, target),
455: 		}
456: 	}
457: }

459: // frontierBaseURL strips the per-endpoint suffix (/chat/completions
460: // is the only supported shape today) from cfg.FrontierURL so we can
461: // hit /v1/models for the key-validation probe. Falls back to the raw
462: // URL when no recognised suffix is present — in that case we issue
463: // the probe against the configured URL itself and let the server
464: // reject it.
465: func frontierBaseURL(raw string) (string, error) {
466: 	if raw == "" {
467: 		return "", fmt.Errorf("empty url")
468: 	}
469: 	u, err := url.Parse(raw)
470: 	if err != nil {
471: 		return "", err
472: 	}
473: 	if !strings.HasSuffix(u.Path, "/chat/completions") {
474: 		return raw, nil
475: 	}
476: 	u.Path = strings.TrimSuffix(u.Path, "/chat/completions")
477: 	return u.String(), nil
478: }

503: // --- VRAM probe ------------------------------------------------------------
504: 
505: // checkVRAMProbeFn drives the Ollama probe directly (no Manager —
506: // the diagnostic command is one-shot and should not spin up a
507: // goroutine) and reports the resulting budget. A non-zero budget is
508: // pass; zero budget (no signal) is warn — the handler falls back to
509: // the static NEXUS_TOKEN_GUARDRAIL in that case, which still serves
510: // traffic but loses the dynamic-aware behaviour the PRD promises.
511: //
512: // When NVIDIA GPUs are detected (issue #775), per-GPU VRAM status is
513: // included in the detail line: "GPU 0: 8.2 GiB free, GPU 1: 8.2 GiB free".
514: func checkVRAMProbeFn(ctx context.Context, cfg config.Config, opts Options) Check {
515: 	p := probe.NewOllamaProbe(opts.OllamaURL, opts.HTTPClient)
516: 	p.BytesPerToken = cfg.ProbeBytesPerToken
517: 	if opts.SysfsRoot != "" {
518: 		p.SysfsRoot = opts.SysfsRoot
519: 	}
520: 	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, opts.Timeout)
521: 	defer cancel()
522: 	b, err := p.Budget(ctx)
523: 	if err != nil {
524: 		return Check{
525: 			Name:   checkVRAMProbe,
526: 			Status: StatusWarn,
527: 			Detail: fmt.Sprintf("probe produced no budget: %v (falling back to NEXUS_TOKEN_GUARDRAIL=%d)", err, cfg.TokenGuardrail),
528: 		}
529: 	}
530: 	if b.Disabled() {
531: 		return Check{
532: 			Name:   checkVRAMProbe,
533: 			Status: StatusWarn,
534: 			Detail: fmt.Sprintf("budget disabled (source=%s) — falling back to NEXUS_TOKEN_GUARDRAIL=%d", b.Source, cfg.TokenGuardrail),
535: 		}
536: 	}
537: 	detail := fmt.Sprintf("budget: %d tokens (source: %s)", b.Tokens, b.Source)
538: 	if gpus, gerr := probe.ReadPerGPUVRAM(); gerr == nil && len(gpus) > 0 {
539: 		var parts []string
540: 		for _, g := range gpus {
541: 			parts = append(parts, fmt.Sprintf("GPU %d: %.1f GiB free", g.Index, float64(g.MemoryFree)/(1024*1024*1024)))
542: 		}
543: 		if len(parts) > 0 {
544: 			detail += "; " + strings.Join(parts, ", ")
545: 		}
546: 	}
547: 	return Check{
548: 		Name:   checkVRAMProbe,
549: 		Status: StatusPass,
550: 		Detail: detail,
551: 	}
552: }

554: // --- RAG examples directory ------------------------------------------------
555: 
556: // checkRAGDirectoryFn inspects cfg.ExamplesDir. A missing directory
557: // is a warning (not a failure) because RAG silently no-ops on an
558: // empty store and the proxy still serves traffic; the operator
559: // simply will not get the few-shot boost.
560: func checkRAGDirectoryFn(cfg config.Config) Check {
561: 	if cfg.ExamplesDir == "" {
562: 		return Check{
563: 			Name:   checkRAGDirectory,
564: 			Status: StatusWarn,
565: 			Detail: "no NEXUS_EXAMPLES_DIR configured",
566: 		}
567: 	}
568: 	info, err := os.Stat(cfg.ExamplesDir)
569: 	if err != nil {
570: 		return Check{
571: 			Name:   checkRAGDirectory,
572: 			Status: StatusWarn,
573: 			Detail: fmt.Sprintf("cannot stat %q: %v", cfg.ExamplesDir, err),
574: 		}
575: 	}
576: 	if !info.IsDir() {
577: 		return Check{
578: 			Name:   checkRAGDirectory,
579: 			Status: StatusWarn,
580: 			Detail: fmt.Sprintf("%q is not a directory", cfg.ExamplesDir),
581: 		}
582: 	}
583: 	entries, err := os.ReadDir(cfg.ExamplesDir)
584: 	if err != nil {
585: 		return Check{
586: 			Name:   checkRAGDirectory,
587: 			Status: StatusWarn,
588: 			Detail: fmt.Sprintf("cannot read %q: %v", cfg.ExamplesDir, err),
589: 		}
590: 	}
591: 	if len(entries) == 0 {
592: 		return Check{
593: 			Name:   checkRAGDirectory,
594: 			Status: StatusWarn,
595: 			Detail: fmt.Sprintf("%q is empty — RAG injection inactive", cfg.ExamplesDir),
596: 		}
597: 	}
598: 	return Check{
599: 		Name:   checkRAGDirectory,
600: 		Status: StatusPass,
601: 		Detail: fmt.Sprintf("%d file(s) in %q", len(entries), cfg.ExamplesDir),
602: 	}
603: }

605: // --- Writable on-disk paths ------------------------------------------------
606: 
607: // checkWritablePathFn tries to os.CreateTemp in the parent directory
608: // of path. An empty path (operator opted out) is reported as skip
609: // — there is nothing to check.
610: func checkWritablePathFn(checkName, path string) Check {
611: 	if path == "" {
612: 		return Check{
613: 			Name:   checkName,
614: 			Status: StatusSkip,
615: 			Detail: "path not configured",
616: 		}
617: 	}
618: 	parent := filepath.Dir(path)
619: 	// filepath.Dir of a bare filename (no slashes) returns "." —
620: 	// the temp-file probe will use the cwd, which is what we want.
621: 	f, err := os.CreateTemp(parent, "nexus-check-*")
622: 	if err != nil {
623: 		return Check{
624: 			Name:   checkName,
625: 			Status: StatusFail,
626: 			Detail: fmt.Sprintf("cannot write to %q: %v", path, err),
627: 		}
628: 	}
629: 	tmpName := f.Name()
630: 	_ = f.Close()
631: 	_ = os.Remove(tmpName)
632: 	return Check{
633: 		Name:   checkName,
634: 		Status: StatusPass,
635: 		Detail: fmt.Sprintf("writable (%s)", path),
636: 	}
637: }

645: // reported as fail — the evaluator would panic on the first call.

650: 			Status: StatusSkip,

659: 		}

668: // --- RAG circuit breaker ---------------------------------------------------
669: 
670: // checkRAGCircuitBreakerFn inspects the RAG circuit breaker threshold.
671: // A threshold of 0 means the breaker is disabled and RAG will retry
672: // indefinitely on failures (no backstop). This is a warning because
673: // a misbehaving embedding endpoint can exhaust proxy resources silently.
674: func checkRAGCircuitBreakerFn(cfg config.Config) Check {
675: 	if cfg.RAGCircuitBreakerThreshold == 0 {
676: 		return Check{

57: //   - outcome: "hit" or "miss"

59: // Total cardinality is 4 series. We pre-allocate one histogram per pair
60: // so ObserveRAGSimilarity is a lock-free single increment — the
61: // histogram map lookup is read-locked but the histogram's Observe
62: // method itself never contends.
63: var ragSimilarityLabels = []struct {
64: 	path    string
65: 	outcome string
66: }{
67: 	{path: "hnsw", outcome: "hit"},
68: 	{path: "hnsw", outcome: "miss"},
69: 	{path: "brute_force", outcome: "hit"},
70: 	{path: "brute_force", outcome: "miss"},
71: }

77: 	"css",
78: 	"refactoring",

86: // ObservabilityEvent is the per-request payload the chat handler
87: // dispatches to the Collector via the ObservabilityObserver hook. Every
88: // proxied request — success or failure — produces exactly one event;
89: // the collector increments its atomics from Submit.
90: //
91: // The type lives here (not in internal/handlers) because it is the
92: // collector's own event surface. handlers imports this leaf package
93: // (no cycle: observability imports nothing internal), so the collector
94: // satisfies handlers.ObservabilityObserver directly and main.go needs
95: // no field-copy adapter.
96: type ObservabilityEvent struct {
97: 	Route string // "local" | "frontier" | "fusion"; unknown values count as frontier
98: 
99: 	// Error is non-empty when the upstream call failed. The collector
100: 	// increments errorsTotal iff Error != "".
101: 	Error string
102: 
103: 	// Routing/optimisation dimensions.
104: 	RAGInjected    bool // a few-shot snippet was injected into the prompt
105: 	TOONCompressed bool // JSON-array blocks were TOON-compressed
106: 	Degraded       bool // local arm was skipped because Ollama was unhealthy
107: 
108: 	// Token + cost accounting (cumulative across the process lifetime).
109: 	InputTokens       int
110: 	OutputTokens      int
111: 	TOONSavingsTokens int
112: 	EstimatedCostUSD  float64
113: 
114: 	// Latency dimensions. TTFTMs is 0 for non-streaming responses.
115: 	TotalLatencyMs int64
116: 	TTFTMs         int64
117: 
118: 	// Per-stage latency breakdown (issue #300). Each field is the
119: 	// wall-clock milliseconds spent in that pipeline stage. 0 when
120: 	// the stage was skipped or not applicable.
121: 	RAGRetrievalMs      int64 // RAG embedding + retrieval
122: 	PromptEngineeringMs int64 // meta-prompt injection
123: 	TOONCompressionMs   int64 // JSON array compression
124: 	SLMRoutingMs        int64 // SLM routing decision (including DSL fast-pass)
125: 	UpstreamFirstByteMs int64 // upstream call to first byte (TTFT minus proxy overhead)
126: 
127: 	// SLM confidence recording (issue #425). Confidence is 0.0..1.0
128: 	// from the judge-guided adaptive routing store; TaskType is the
129: 	// Categorize() bucket. Both are zero when the SLM was not
130: 	// consulted (guardrail/DSL stages) or on cache hits.
131: 	SLMConfidence float64
132: 	SLMTaskType   string
133: }

135: // Collector is the in-process metrics surface. It is safe for
136: // concurrent use: every field is a sync/atomic primitive, so the
137: // request path (Submit) and the scrape path (Snapshot / RenderPrometheus)
138: // never contend on a lock. The scrape handler completes in well under a
139: // millisecond regardless of how many samples have accumulated.
140: type Collector struct {
141: 	// Per-route request counters. Rendered with a route label so a
142: 	// single PromQL query can break traffic down by destination.
143: 	requestsLocal    atomic.Uint64
144: 	requestsFrontier atomic.Uint64
145: 	requestsFusion   atomic.Uint64
146: 
147: 	// Per-route error counters (issue #120).
148: 	errorsLocal    atomic.Uint64
149: 	errorsFrontier atomic.Uint64
150: 	errorsFusion   atomic.Uint64
151: 
152: 	ragHitsTotal           atomic.Uint64
153: 	ragMissesTotal         atomic.Uint64
154: 	toonCompressedTotal    atomic.Uint64
155: 	degradedTotal          atomic.Uint64
156: 	inputTokensTotal       atomic.Uint64
157: 	outputTokensTotal      atomic.Uint64
158: 	toonSavingsTokensTotal atomic.Uint64
159: 
160: 	// estimatedCostUSDBits holds the cumulative USD cost as its
161: 	// IEEE-754 bit pattern in an atomic.Uint64
162: 	// (math.Float64bits / Float64frombits) so the hot path can
163: 	// accumulate a float without a mutex.
164: 	estimatedCostUSDBits atomic.Uint64
165: 
166: 	// Per-route latency and TTFT histograms (issue #120).
167: 	latencyLocal    *Histogram
168: 	latencyFrontier *Histogram
169: 	latencyFusion   *Histogram
170: 	ttftLocal       *Histogram
171: 	ttftFrontier    *Histogram
172: 	ttftFusion      *Histogram
173: 
174: 	// Per-stage pipeline latency histograms (issue #300).
175: 	// Labelled by stage: rag, prompt_eng, toon, slm, upstream.
176: 	stageRAG       *Histogram
177: 	stagePromptEng *Histogram
178: 	stageTOON      *Histogram
179: 	stageSLM       *Histogram
180: 	stageUpstream  *Histogram
181: 
182: 	// --- Middleware instrumentation (issue #70) ---------------------------
183: 	//
184: 	// Auth counters are labelled by outcome via three separate atomics
185: 	// rather than a label-keyed map. The label set is fixed at three
186: 	// values, so three atomics is the simplest lock-free layout and
187: 	// keeps the hot path to a single add per request.
188: 	authAccepted        atomic.Uint64
189: 	authRejectedInvalid atomic.Uint64
190: 	authRejectedMissing atomic.Uint64
191: 
192: 	// Auth limiter reaper evictions counter (issue #839). Incremented
193: 	// each time the reaper goroutine evicts an idle IP from the
194: 	// failures map.
195: 	authReaperEvictions atomic.Uint64
196: 
197: 	// Auth limiter blocked counter (issue #831). Incremented each time
198: 	// an IP is blocked (burst threshold crossed) by the auth limiter.
199: 	authBlockedTotal atomic.Uint64
200: 
201: 	// Rate-limit counters are emitted per bucket (global / per_client)
202: 	// so operators can tell at a glance whether the global bucket or a
203: 	// specific client is the bottleneck (issue #70 AC: "How many
204: 	// requests are 429'd by the rate limiter (per client IP and
205: 	// globally)?").
206: 	rateLimitAllowedGlobal     atomic.Uint64
207: 	rateLimitAllowedPerClient  atomic.Uint64
208: 	rateLimitRejectedGlobal    atomic.Uint64
209: 	rateLimitRejectedPerClient atomic.Uint64
210: 
211: 	// Budget counters track daily frontier spend (issue #38).
212: 	// Exceeded is bumped when the gate rejects; RecordedUSD is the
213: 	// running sum (float, lock-free via the bits trick) of amounts
214: 	// the tracker recorded after a frontier call completed.
215: 	budgetExceededTotal   atomic.Uint64
216: 	budgetRecordedUSDBits atomic.Uint64
217: 
218: 	// TLS counters are bumped from main.go via http.Server.ConnState.
219: 	// Accepted fires on http.StateTLSHandshakeComplete; Rejected
220: 	// fires when a connection closes before reaching that state.
221: 	tlsConnectionsAccepted atomic.Uint64
222: 	tlsConnectionsRejected atomic.Uint64
223: 
224: 	// --- Circuit breaker instrumentation (issue #304) ---------------
225: 	//
226: 	// Tracks the state of each named circuit breaker (ollama, rag).
227: 	// State values: 0=closed, 1=half_open, 2=open.
228: 	// Protected by cbMu; read via atomic for hot path.
229: 	cbMu    sync.RWMutex
230: 	cbState map[string]*circuitBreakerState
231: 
232: 	// --- SLM confidence histogram (issue #425) --------------------
233: 	//
234: 	// Per-task-category confidence histograms. Maps category name to
235: 	// histogram. Pre-allocated in NewCollector so ObserveSLMConfidence
236: 	// only needs a read lock to find the histogram; the histogram's
237: 	// Observe method itself is lock-free.
238: 	slmConfidenceMu         sync.RWMutex
239: 	slmConfidenceHistograms map[string]*Histogram
240: 
241: 	// --- RAG similarity histogram (issue #447) -------------------
242: 	//
243: 	// Per-(path, outcome) cosine-similarity histograms. The (path,
244: 	// outcome) label set is fixed at 4 pairs (see ragSimilarityLabels)
245: 	// so we pre-allocate the histograms in NewCollector and never
246: 	// mutate the map after boot. ObserveRAGSimilarity only needs a
247: 	// read lock to find the histogram; Histogram.Observe is lock-free.
248: 	ragSimilarityMu         sync.RWMutex
249: 	ragSimilarityHistograms map[string]*Histogram // keyed by "path|outcome"
250: 
251: 	// --- Rate-limit bucket utilization histogram (issue #746) --------
252: 	//
253: 	// Per-bucket-ID utilization histograms. Each histogram records the
254: 	// fractional token utilization (tokens/burst) at the moment of
255: 	// acquisition. Histograms are created lazily per bucket so the
256: 	// hot path is a single read-lock + map lookup; Histogram.Observe
257: 	// itself is lock-free.
258: 	rateLimitUtilizationMu         sync.RWMutex
259: 	rateLimitUtilizationHistograms map[string]*Histogram // keyed by bucketID (hashed IP)
260: 
261: 	// --- Embedder circuit breaker instrumentation (issue #423) -----
262: 	//
263: 	// Tracks failures for each embedder circuit breaker (ollama, rag).
264: 	// Protected by cbMu for map access; individual counters are atomic.
265: 	embedderMu       sync.RWMutex
266: 	embedderFailures map[string]*atomic.Uint64 // keyed by "ollama", "openai", "cohere"
267: 
268: 	// --- Per-route latency percentile ring buffers (issue #774) --------
269: 	//
270: 	// Per-(route) sliding window ring buffers that store recent latency
271: 	// samples and maintain running p50/p95/p99 estimates. Keyed by route
272: 	// string ("local", "frontier", "fusion").
273: 	latencyPercentilesMu sync.RWMutex
274: 	latencyPercentiles   map[string]*latencyPercentileBuffer
275: }

277: // circuitBreakerState holds the atomic state for one named circuit.
278: type circuitBreakerState struct {
279: 	state       atomic.Int32 // 0=closed, 1=half_open, 2=open
280: 	failures    atomic.Uint64
281: 	lastFailure atomic.Int64 // Unix timestamp (seconds) of last failure
282: }

284: const (
285: 	circuitStateClosed   int32 = 0
286: 	circuitStateHalfOpen int32 = 1
287: 	circuitStateOpen     int32 = 2
288: )

290: // NewCollector constructs a Collector with the default latency and TTFT
291: // histograms for each route and per-stage pipeline histograms (issue #300).
292: // The returned collector is ready to receive Submit calls and
293: // RenderPrometheus scrapes from any goroutine.
294: func NewCollector() *Collector {
295: 	c := &Collector{
296: 		latencyLocal:     NewHistogram(DefaultBuckets),
297: 		latencyFrontier:  NewHistogram(DefaultBuckets),
298: 		latencyFusion:    NewHistogram(DefaultBuckets),
299: 		ttftLocal:        NewHistogram(DefaultBuckets),
300: 		ttftFrontier:     NewHistogram(DefaultBuckets),
301: 		ttftFusion:       NewHistogram(DefaultBuckets),
302: 		stageRAG:         NewHistogram(DefaultBuckets),
303: 		stagePromptEng:   NewHistogram(DefaultBuckets),
304: 		stageTOON:        NewHistogram(DefaultBuckets),
305: 		stageSLM:         NewHistogram(DefaultBuckets),
306: 		stageUpstream:    NewHistogram(DefaultBuckets),
307: 		embedderFailures: make(map[string]*atomic.Uint64),
308: 	}
309: 	// Pre-allocate SLM confidence histograms for each known category
310: 	// (issue #425). Pre-allocation means ObserveSLMConfidence only
311: 	// needs a read lock to find the histogram; Histogram.Observe
312: 	// itself is lock-free.
313: 	c.slmConfidenceHistograms = make(map[string]*Histogram, len(slmConfidenceCategories))
314: 	for _, cat := range slmConfidenceCategories {
315: 		c.slmConfidenceHistograms[cat] = NewHistogram(ConfidenceBuckets)
316: 	}
317: 	// Pre-allocate RAG similarity histograms for the default (path, outcome)
318: 	// pairs (issue #447). Additional histograms for per-threshold observations
319: 	// are created lazily by ObserveRAGSimilarity (issue #671).
320: 	c.ragSimilarityHistograms = make(map[string]*Histogram, len(ragSimilarityLabels))
321: 	for _, l := range ragSimilarityLabels {
322: 		key := ragSimilarityKey(l.path, l.outcome, 0) // 0 = default/global threshold
323: 		c.ragSimilarityHistograms[key] = NewHistogram(RAGSimilarityBuckets)
324: 	}
325: 	return c
326: }
327: 
328: // ragSimilarityKey builds the lookup key for the (path, outcome, threshold) tuple.
329: // Stable across processes so scrape diffs are reproducible.
330: // The threshold is rounded to 2 decimal places to avoid floating-point
331: // key explosion while still providing per-threshold visibility (issue #671).
332: func ragSimilarityKey(path, outcome string, threshold float64) string {
333: 	return fmt.Sprintf("%s|%s|%.2f", path, outcome, threshold)
334: }

336: // Submit records one ObservabilityEvent. Called exactly once per
337: // proxied request from the chat handler's request goroutine. Submit is
338: // a sequence of atomic increments — it never blocks, never allocates,
339: // and is safe to call from many goroutines concurrently.
340: func (c *Collector) Submit(e ObservabilityEvent) {
341: 	var latencyHist *Histogram
342: 	var ttftHist *Histogram
343: 	switch e.Route {
344: 	case "local":
345: 		c.requestsLocal.Add(1)
346: 		if e.Error != "" {
347: 			c.errorsLocal.Add(1)
348: 		}
349: 		latencyHist = c.latencyLocal
350: 		ttftHist = c.ttftLocal
351: 	case "fusion":
352: 		c.requestsFusion.Add(1)
353: 		if e.Error != "" {
354: 			c.errorsFusion.Add(1)
355: 		}
356: 		latencyHist = c.latencyFusion
357: 		ttftHist = c.ttftFusion
358: 	default: // "frontier" and any unrecognised route count as frontier
359: 		c.requestsFrontier.Add(1)
360: 		if e.Error != "" {
361: 			c.errorsFrontier.Add(1)
362: 		}
363: 		latencyHist = c.latencyFrontier
364: 		ttftHist = c.ttftFrontier
365: 	}
366: 	if e.RAGInjected {
367: 		c.ragHitsTotal.Add(1)
368: 	} else {
369: 		c.ragMissesTotal.Add(1)
370: 	}
371: 	if e.TOONCompressed {
372: 		c.toonCompressedTotal.Add(1)
373: 	}
374: 	if e.Degraded {
375: 		c.degradedTotal.Add(1)
376: 	}
377: 	if e.InputTokens > 0 {
378: 		c.inputTokensTotal.Add(uint64(e.InputTokens))
379: 	}
380: 	if e.OutputTokens > 0 {
381: 		c.outputTokensTotal.Add(uint64(e.OutputTokens))
382: 	}
383: 	if e.TOONSavingsTokens > 0 {
384: 		c.toonSavingsTokensTotal.Add(uint64(e.TOONSavingsTokens))
385: 	}
386: 	if e.EstimatedCostUSD > 0 {
387: 		atomicAddFloat(&c.estimatedCostUSDBits, e.EstimatedCostUSD)
388: 	}
389: 	if e.TotalLatencyMs > 0 && latencyHist != nil {
390: 		latencyHist.Observe(float64(e.TotalLatencyMs))
391: 	}
392: 	if e.TTFTMs > 0 && ttftHist != nil {
393: 		ttftHist.Observe(float64(e.TTFTMs))
394: 	}
395: 	// Per-stage pipeline latency histograms (issue #300).
396: 	if e.RAGRetrievalMs > 0 {
397: 		c.stageRAG.Observe(float64(e.RAGRetrievalMs))
398: 	}
399: 	if e.PromptEngineeringMs > 0 {
400: 		c.stagePromptEng.Observe(float64(e.PromptEngineeringMs))
401: 	}
402: 	if e.TOONCompressionMs > 0 {
403: 		c.stageTOON.Observe(float64(e.TOONCompressionMs))
404: 	}
405: 	if e.SLMRoutingMs > 0 {
406: 		c.stageSLM.Observe(float64(e.SLMRoutingMs))
407: 	}
408: 	if e.UpstreamFirstByteMs > 0 {
409: 		c.stageUpstream.Observe(float64(e.UpstreamFirstByteMs))
410: 	}
411: 	// SLM confidence histogram (issue #425). Recorded when both
412: 	// Confidence > 0 and TaskType is a known category. A zero
413: 	// confidence means the SLM was not consulted (guardrail/DSL
414: 	// path); an empty TaskType means cache hit or no confidence
415: 	// store was wired.
416: 	if e.SLMConfidence > 0 && e.SLMTaskType != "" {
417: 		c.ObserveSLMConfidence(e.SLMTaskType, e.SLMConfidence)
418: 	}
419: }

462: // ObserveLatency records a latency observation for percentile computation
463: // (issue #774). route is the routing decision ("local", "frontier", "fusion").
464: // latencyMs is the total request latency in milliseconds. Safe for concurrent use.
465: func (c *Collector) ObserveLatency(route string, latencyMs int64) {
466: 	if c == nil || latencyMs <= 0 {
467: 		return
468: 	}
469: 	c.latencyPercentilesMu.RLock()
470: 	buf, ok := c.latencyPercentiles[route]
471: 	c.latencyPercentilesMu.RUnlock()
472: 	if ok && buf != nil {
473: 		buf.Observe(float64(latencyMs))
474: 		return
475: 	}
476: 	// Lazily create buffer
477: 	c.latencyPercentilesMu.Lock()
478: 	if c.latencyPercentiles == nil {
479: 		c.latencyPercentiles = make(map[string]*latencyPercentileBuffer)
480: 	}
481: 	buf, ok = c.latencyPercentiles[route]
482: 	if !ok || buf == nil {
483: 		buf = newLatencyPercentileBuffer(defaultLatencyBufferCapacity)
484: 		c.latencyPercentiles[route] = buf
485: 	}
486: 	c.latencyPercentilesMu.Unlock()
487: 	buf.Observe(float64(latencyMs))
488: }

490: // LatencyPercentileGauges returns the current p50/p95/p99 latency readings
491: // per route as GaugeSamples for the Prometheus renderer. Values are 0 when
492: // no samples have been recorded for a route.
493: func (c *Collector) LatencyPercentileGauges() []GaugeSample {
494: 	if c == nil {
495: 		return nil
496: 	}
497: 	c.latencyPercentilesMu.RLock()
498: 	defer c.latencyPercentilesMu.RUnlock()
499: 	var out []GaugeSample
500: 	// Fixed route order for deterministic output
501: 	for _, route := range []string{"local", "frontier", "fusion"} {
502: 		buf := c.latencyPercentiles[route]
503: 		if buf == nil {
504: 			continue
505: 		}
506: 		p50, p95, p99 := buf.Perc()
507: 		labels := map[string]string{"route": route}
508: 		out = append(out,
509: 			GaugeSample{Name: "nexus_upstream_request_latency_p50_seconds", Labels: labels, Value: p50 / 1000}, // ms → s
510: 			GaugeSample{Name: "nexus_upstream_request_latency_p95_seconds", Labels: labels, Value: p95 / 1000},
511: 			GaugeSample{Name: "nexus_upstream_request_latency_p99_seconds", Labels: labels, Value: p99 / 1000},
512: 		)
513: 	}
514: 	return out
515: }

517: // --- Middleware instrumentation helpers (issue #70) ----------------------
518: //
519: // Each helper bumps exactly one atomic counter so the middleware hot
520: // path stays a single atomic add. The middleware packages own the
521: // decision logic (when a request is "accepted" vs "rejected_invalid"
522: // etc.); the collector only stores the resulting counts.
523: 
524: // IncAuthAccepted records one accepted authentication request.
525: func (c *Collector) IncAuthAccepted() { c.authAccepted.Add(1) }
526: 
527: // IncAuthRejectedInvalid records a request that presented a
528: // credential but it did not match any configured key.
529: func (c *Collector) IncAuthRejectedInvalid() { c.authRejectedInvalid.Add(1) }
530: 
531: // IncAuthRejectedMissing records a request that presented no
532: // credential at all (no Authorization / X-API-Key header).
533: func (c *Collector) IncAuthRejectedMissing() { c.authRejectedMissing.Add(1) }
534: 
535: // IncAuthReaperEvictions records one reaper eviction of an idle IP
536: // from the auth limiter's failures map (issue #839).
537: func (c *Collector) IncAuthReaperEvictions() { c.authReaperEvictions.Add(1) }
538: 
539: // IncAuthBlocked records one auth limiter block event — an IP that
540: // crossed the burst threshold and is now blocked (issue #831).
541: func (c *Collector) IncAuthBlocked() { c.authBlockedTotal.Add(1) }
542: 
543: // AuthAuthenticatedClients returns the cumulative count of accepted
544: // authentications. The /metrics renderer exposes it under the gauge
545: // name nexus_auth_authenticated_clients so operators can chart a
546: // running total of successful auth events without scraping logs.
547: //
548: // (The name carries "clients" rather than "events" because the issue
549: // spec calls for a gauge by that name; semantically this is a
550: // monotonic counter rendered as a gauge family so a single PromQL
551: // query shows the long-running trend.)
552: func (c *Collector) AuthAuthenticatedClients() uint64 { return c.authAccepted.Load() }
553: 
554: // IncRateLimit bumps the appropriate rate-limit counter for scope
555: // (one of "global", "per_client"). The middleware packages own the
556: // mapping from configuration to scope label.
557: //
558: // A scope other than "global" or "per_client" is silently ignored
559: // rather than treated as a default — the renderer only knows those
560: // two label values, so a third bucket would be invisible. Invalid
561: // scopes indicate a wiring bug worth surfacing in logs at the call
562: // site rather than silently dropping.
563: func (c *Collector) IncRateLimit(scope string, allowed bool) {
564: 	switch scope {
565: 	case "global":
566: 		if allowed {
567: 			c.rateLimitAllowedGlobal.Add(1)
568: 		} else {
569: 			c.rateLimitRejectedGlobal.Add(1)
570: 		}
571: 	case "per_client":
572: 		if allowed {
573: 			c.rateLimitAllowedPerClient.Add(1)
574: 		} else {
575: 			c.rateLimitRejectedPerClient.Add(1)
576: 		}
577: 	}
578: }

922: // --- Per-route latency percentile ring buffers (issue #774) -----------
923: //
924: // latencyPercentileBuffer stores a sliding window of latency samples and
925: // maintains running p50/p95/p99 percentile estimates. Updated on each
926: // request completion so percentiles are always current at scrape time.
927: // The ring buffer has fixed capacity; oldest samples are evicted.
928: //
929: // Using a ring buffer (not histogram interpolation) gives exact
930: // percentile values from actual samples — operators can set precise
931: // SLO alerts (e.g. "p95 < 2s") without client-side queries.
932: //
933: // Capacity of 1000 samples gives ~3–15 min of history depending on
934: // request rate, sufficient for stable p95/p99 estimates.
935: type latencyPercentileBuffer struct {
936: 	mu       sync.Mutex
937: 	samples  []float64 // latency in milliseconds, oldest first
938: 	capacity int
939: 	p50Bits  atomic.Uint64 // IEEE-754 bits of p50 value
940: 	p95Bits  atomic.Uint64
941: 	p99Bits  atomic.Uint64
942: }
943: 
944: const defaultLatencyBufferCapacity = 1000
945: 
946: func newLatencyPercentileBuffer(capacity int) *latencyPercentileBuffer {
947: 	if capacity <= 0 {
948: 		capacity = defaultLatencyBufferCapacity
949: 	}
950: 	return &latencyPercentileBuffer{
951: 		samples:  make([]float64, 0, capacity),
952: 		capacity: capacity,
953: 	}
954: }
955: 
956: func (b *latencyPercentileBuffer) Observe(latencyMs float64) {
957: 	b.mu.Lock()
958: 	defer b.mu.Unlock()
959: 
960: 	if len(b.samples) < b.capacity {
961: 		b.samples = append(b.samples, latencyMs)
962: 	} else {
963: 		// Ring buffer: overwrite oldest, keep newest
964: 		copy(b.samples, b.samples[1:])
965: 		b.samples[b.capacity-1] = latencyMs
966: 	}
967: 
968: 	b.recomputePercentilesLocked()
969: }
970: 
971: func (b *latencyPercentileBuffer) recomputePercentilesLocked() {
972: 	n := len(b.samples)
973: 	if n == 0 {
974: 		return
975: 	}
976: 	// Sort ascending for percentile computation
977: 	sorted := make([]float64, n)
978: 	copy(sorted, b.samples)
979: 	sort.Float64s(sorted)
980: 
981: 	b.p50Bits.Store(math.Float64bits(percentile(sorted, 0.50)))
982: 	b.p95Bits.Store(math.Float64bits(percentile(sorted, 0.95)))
983: 	b.p99Bits.Store(math.Float64bits(percentile(sorted, 0.99)))
984: }
985: 
986: func percentile(sorted []float64, p float64) float64 {
987: 	if len(sorted) == 0 {
988: 		return 0
989: 	}
990: 	if len(sorted) == 1 {
991: 		return sorted[0]
992: 	}
993: 	// Linear interpolation between nearest ranks
994: 	idx := p * float64(len(sorted)-1)
995: 	lower := int(idx)
996: 	upper := lower + 1
997: 	if upper >= len(sorted) {
998: 		return sorted[len(sorted)-1]
999: 	}
1000: 	frac := idx - float64(lower)
1001: 	return sorted[lower]*(1-frac) + sorted[upper]*frac
1002: }

1004: // Perc returns the current p50/p95/p99 readings. Values are 0 when
1005: // no samples have been recorded yet.
1006: func (b *latencyPercentileBuffer) Perc() (p50, p95, p99 float64) {
1007: 	return math.Float64frombits(b.p50Bits.Load()),
1008: 		math.Float64frombits(b.p95Bits.Load()),
1009: 		math.Float64frombits(b.p99Bits.Load())
1010: }

1013: func (b *latencyPercentileBuffer) Count() int {
1014: 	b.mu.Lock()

1016: 	return len(b.samples)

1019: // Histogram is a fixed-bucket cumulative histogram. Buckets are
1020: // pre-allocated at construction; Observe performs a single linear scan
1021: // over the finite upper bounds (at most one atomic increment) plus the
1022: // running sum/count, so it is allocation-free on the hot path.
1023: //
1024: // Per-bucket counts are stored non-cumulatively; the cumulative counts
1025: // required by the Prometheus exposition format are derived at render
1026: // time (Snapshot). This keeps Observe to a single increment regardless
1027: // of bucket count.
1028: type Histogram struct {
1029: 	upperBounds []float64       // finite upper bounds, ascending
1030: 	counts      []atomic.Uint64 // len == len(upperBounds)+1; last is the +Inf overflow bucket
1031: 	sumBits     atomic.Uint64   // float64 bits (math.Float64bits)
1032: 	count       atomic.Uint64   // total observations
1033: }
1034: 
1035: // NewHistogram constructs a Histogram whose finite buckets are bounded
1036: // by upperBounds (ascending). A trailing +Inf bucket is implicit.
1037: func NewHistogram(upperBounds []float64) *Histogram {
1038: 	return &Histogram{
1039: 		upperBounds: upperBounds,
1040: 		counts:      make([]atomic.Uint64, len(upperBounds)+1),
1041: 	}
1042: }
1043: 
1044: // Observe records a single observation. The value lands in the first
1045: // bucket whose upper bound is >= v, or in the trailing +Inf bucket when
1046: // v exceeds every finite bound. Observe is safe for concurrent use.
1047: func (h *Histogram) Observe(v float64) {
1048: 	for i, ub := range h.upperBounds {
1049: 		if v <= ub {
1050: 			h.counts[i].Add(1)
1051: 			h.count.Add(1)
1052: 			atomicAddFloat(&h.sumBits, v)
1053: 			return
1054: 		}
1055: 	}
1056: 	h.counts[len(h.upperBounds)].Add(1)
1057: 	h.count.Add(1)
1058: 	atomicAddFloat(&h.sumBits, v)
1059: }
1060: 
1061: // UpperBounds returns the finite bucket upper bounds. The returned
1062: // slice aliases the histogram's internal storage; callers must not
1063: // mutate it.
1064: func (h *Histogram) UpperBounds() []float64 { return h.upperBounds }
1065: 
1066: // Snapshot returns the cumulative bucket counts, the finite upper
1067: // bounds, the total sum, and the total observation count for rendering.
1068: // The cumulative slice is freshly allocated so the caller never races a
1069: // concurrent Observe.
1070: //
1071: // cumulative[i] holds the count of observations <= upperBounds[i]; the
1072: // final entry (index len(upperBounds)) is the +Inf bucket and equals
1073: // the total observation count.
1074: func (h *Histogram) Snapshot() (cumulative []uint64, upperBounds []float64, sum float64, count uint64) {
1075: 	cumulative = make([]uint64, len(h.upperBounds)+1)
1076: 	var running uint64
1077: 	for i := range h.upperBounds {
1078: 		running += h.counts[i].Load()
1079: 		cumulative[i] = running
1080: 	}
1081: 	running += h.counts[len(h.upperBounds)].Load()
1082: 	cumulative[len(h.upperBounds)] = running
1083: 	upperBounds = h.upperBounds
1084: 	sum = math.Float64frombits(h.sumBits.Load())
1085: 	count = h.count.Load()
1086: 	return
1087: }
1088: 
1089: // atomicAddFloat adds delta to the float64 whose IEEE-754 bits live in
1090: // addr, using a compare-and-swap loop so the hot path stays lock-free.
1091: // Contention is essentially nil in practice (one add per request), so
1092: // the retry loop virtually never spins.
1093: func atomicAddFloat(addr *atomic.Uint64, delta float64) {
1094: 	for {
1095: 		old := addr.Load()
1096: 		newVal := math.Float64frombits(old) + delta
1097: 		if addr.CompareAndSwap(old, math.Float64bits(newVal)) {
1098: 			return
1099: 		}
1100: 	}
1101: }

1: // Subcommand: `nexus check` (alias `nexus doctor`). Runs the boot-
2: // time diagnostic suite defined in internal/diag, prints the result
3: // in either a human-readable table or a JSON array, and exits 0 when
4: // every check passed (warn + skip are fine) or 1 when at least one
5: // check failed.
6: //
7: // This file is the CLI adapter; the actual check logic lives in
8: // internal/diag. Keeping the two separate means a future operator
9: // tool (a TUI, a HTTP /diagz endpoint) can drive the same suite
10: // without re-implementing the wiring.
11: package main
12: 
13: import (
14: 	"context"
15: 	"encoding/json"
16: 	"errors"
17: 	"flag"
18: 	"fmt"
19: 	"io"
20: 	"time"
21: 
22: 	"github.com/anchapin/nexus-proxy/internal/config"
23: 	"github.com/anchapin/nexus-proxy/internal/diag"
24: )
25: 
26: // checkUsage is shown on -h / bad flags. Kept compact because the
27: // proxy is an operator tool, not an end-user app.
28: const checkUsage = `nexus check — boot-time configuration diagnostics for the Nexus Proxy.
29: 
30: Usage:
31:   nexus check [--json]
32: 
33: Flags:
34:   --json              Emit a JSON array of check results instead of a
35:                       human-readable table.
36: 
37: Exit code is 0 when every check passed (warn + skip are fine), 1 when
38: at least one check failed.
39: 
40: Aliases: nexus doctor.
41: `
42: 
43: // runCheck is the testable core of the `nexus check` subcommand.
44: // args and stdout/stderr are parameters so a future test can drive
45: // the full CLI end-to-end. The function returns a process exit code
46: // (0 or 1) rather than calling os.Exit so tests can assert against
47: // it without spawning a subprocess.
48: func runCheck(args []string, stdout, stderr io.Writer) int {
49: 	fs := flag.NewFlagSet("nexus check", flag.ContinueOnError)
50: 	fs.SetOutput(stderr)
51: 	fs.Usage = func() { fmt.Fprint(stderr, checkUsage) }
52: 
53: 	var asJSON bool
54: 	fs.BoolVar(&asJSON, "json", false, "emit JSON instead of a human-readable table")
55: 
56: 	if err := fs.Parse(args); err != nil {
57: 		// flag.ContinueOnError already printed the error and Usage.
58: 		// flag.ErrHelp is the sentinel for -h/--help: the Usage was
59: 		// rendered, the caller wanted information, so exit 0 rather
60: 		// than 1 (matches every other CLI's behaviour).
61: 		if errors.Is(err, flag.ErrHelp) {
62: 			return 0
63: 		}
64: 		return 1
65: 	}
66: 
67: 	cfg, err := config.Load()
68: 	if err != nil {
69: 		fmt.Fprintf(stderr, "nexus check: config: %v\n", err)
70: 		return 1
71: 	}
72: 
73: 	// Use a bounded timeout so a single hung endpoint cannot stall
74: 	// the whole command past the 10-second acceptance criterion.
75: 	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 15*time.Second)
76: 	defer cancel()
77: 
78: 	res := diag.Run(ctx, cfg, diag.Options{
79: 		Timeout: 5 * time.Second,
80: 	})
81: 
82: 	if asJSON {
83: 		if err := renderCheckJSON(res, stdout); err != nil {
84: 			fmt.Fprintf(stderr, "nexus check: %v\n", err)
85: 			return 1
86: 		}
87: 	} else {
88: 		renderCheckTable(res, stdout)
89: 	}
90: 
91: 	if res.Failed() > 0 {
92: 		return 1
93: 	}
94: 	return 0
95: }
96: 
97: // renderCheckTable emits the canonical human-readable report:
98: //
99: //	Nexus Proxy — Configuration Check
100: //	===================================
101: //	[PASS] Ollama reachable at http://localhost:11434
102: //	[FAIL] Model 'nomic-embed-text' not pulled → Run: ollama pull nomic-embed-text
103: //	...
104: //
105: //	1 check failed, 1 warning.
106: func renderCheckTable(r diag.Result, w io.Writer) {
107: 	fmt.Fprintln(w, "Nexus Proxy — Configuration Check")
108: 	fmt.Fprintln(w, "===================================")
109: 	for _, c := range r {
110: 		fmt.Fprintf(w, "[%s] %s\n", statusLabel(c.Status), formatDetail(c))
111: 	}
112: 	failed := r.Failed()
113: 	warned := r.Warned()
114: 	switch {
115: 	case failed > 0 && warned > 0:
116: 		fmt.Fprintf(w, "\n%d check(s) failed, %d warning(s).\n", failed, warned)
117: 	case failed > 0:
118: 		fmt.Fprintf(w, "\n%d check(s) failed.\n", failed)
119: 	case warned > 0:
120: 		fmt.Fprintf(w, "\nAll checks passed, %d warning(s).\n", warned)
121: 	default:
122: 		fmt.Fprintln(w, "\nAll checks passed.")
123: 	}
124: }
125: 
126: // statusLabel renders the four-state status as the bracketed tag
127: // used in both the table and (when piped to a terminal) the exit
128: // status header. Kept uppercase for visual scanning.
129: func statusLabel(s diag.Status) string {
130: 	switch s {
131: 	case diag.StatusPass:
132: 		return "PASS"
133: 	case diag.StatusFail:
134: 		return "FAIL"
135: 	case diag.StatusWarn:
136: 		return "WARN"
137: 	default:
138: 		return "SKIP"
139: 	}
140: }
141: 
142: // formatDetail maps a Check onto the "Name — detail" string the
143: // table prints. Skipped checks get a quieter phrasing so the report
144: // does not look like every step failed.
145: func formatDetail(c diag.Check) string {
146: 	if c.Detail == "" {
147: 		return c.Name
148: 	}
149: 	if c.Status == diag.StatusSkip {
150: 		return fmt.Sprintf("%s — %s", c.Name, c.Detail)
151: 	}
152: 	return fmt.Sprintf("%s — %s", c.Name, c.Detail)
153: }
154: 
155: // renderCheckJSON emits a JSON array of Check objects. The shape is
156: // stable (matches diag.Check's tagged fields) so CI scripts can
157: // pipe the output through `jq` without surprises.
158: func renderCheckJSON(r diag.Result, w io.Writer) error {
159: 	enc := json.NewEncoder(w)
160: 	enc.SetIndent("", "  ")
161: 	return enc.Encode(r)
162: }

1301: // boolFieldDefault applies a default when the YAML field was the zero value.
1302: // Since we cannot distinguish unset from explicit false with a plain bool,
1303: // this is only safe for fields whose default is also false. For fields with
1304: // default=true (fusion_progressive_delivery, models_endpoint_enabled), the
1305: // toConfig() caller must use the YAML value directly when non-zero (which
1306: // in practice means: the YAML value was explicitly set to true).
1307: func (yc YAMLConfig) boolFieldDefault(field, def bool) bool {
1308: 	// Go's zero value for bool is false. If field==false and def==true,
1309: 	// we cannot tell if YAML explicitly set it to false or left it unset.
1310: 	// We resolve this by treating false==def as "use default".
1311: 	if field == def {
1312: 		return def
1313: 	}
1314: 	return field
1315: }
